in_latin.name: Silvanus
in_latin.meaning: nomen Christianum, significat: pax, caritas, bonum
in_latin.long_meaning: Silvanus est nomen Christianum, quod significat pacem, caritatem, et bonum. Origine, nomen venit a nomine Latinum Silvanus, qui significat silvanus, silvaticus. In Ecclesia, nomen est usitatum, et in multis culturis, nomen est significativum paxis et caritatis.

historical_references.reference: Saint Silvia, also known as Silvia of Cologne, was a 7th-century Frankish princess and a Christian saint. She was the sister of Pepin of Landen and the mother of Pippin of Herstal, who became the first Carolingian king of the Franks. Silvia is venerated as a patron saint of Cologne, Germany.

Silvian, or Silvia, was a Christian martyr from the 4th century in the Roman province of Dalmatia, now Croatia. According to legend, she was a noblewoman who was persecuted for her faith and was eventually put to death. Her feast day is celebrated on January 27.
